Title: Vasovagal Syncope: The Sudden Blackout After Donating Blood

Description:
Red Cross donor data show fainting risk is highest in young, first-time blood donors — 16-17 year olds faint at more than 3x the rate of donors over 20, and over half of all donor fainting reactions happen in people 22 or younger. It happens because your vagus nerve overreacts to a trigger (blood, needles, pain, prolonged standing), dropping your heart rate and blood pressure at once.

Four habits cut your risk: recognize the warning signs and sit or lie down fast, use physical counterpressure moves (a JACC trial cut recurrence from 51% to 32%), stay hydrated with enough salt, and plan ahead for known triggers.
